Public Comments

Please email all public comments to Lhakobian@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line of
your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business) and
Item Number you are commenting on. The Staff will read public comments into the record for up to the
three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read.

   MINUTES OF JUNE 7, 2021
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Cabot called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to order
at 6:31 P.M. on Monday, June 7, 2021, with Commissioners and staff participating by
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Chair Cabot.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Cheryl Anne Cabot, Catherine Cordero, Theresa Huerta,
  Bronwyn Velazquez and Ting Xie.
Commissioners Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  Community Services Manager, Lucy Hakobian,
  Community Services Supervisor, Christina Alatorre and
  Commission Secretary, Adrienne Franquez.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Chair Cabot announced the agenda order was approved.

2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. WELCOME OF NEW COMMISSIONERS
  Community Services Manager, Lucy Hakobian made the presentation.

  B. COVID-19 BRIEFING
  Community Services Manager, Lucy Hakobian made the presentation.

  C. COMMISSION AWARD

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  JUNE 7, 2021
   Community Services Supervisor, Christina Alatorre made the presentation.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT – Comment made by Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nunez. Provided
  information regarding new HEAR Commission. First meeting was held on April 28th
  and she looks forward to partnering with community organizations and city
  commissions to promote respect, appreciation and acknowledgment for diversity in
  the City of San Gabriel.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A. APPROVAL MINUTES

  A motion was made by Vice-Chair Velazquez, seconded by Commissioner Huerta to
  approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for May 3, 2021.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 3-0-2 as follows:

  AYES:  VELAZQUEZ, HUERTA, CABOT
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  CORDERO, XIE
  ABSENT:  NONE

5. ACTION ITEMS

  A. COMMISSIONER REORGANIZATION
  Community Services Manager, Lucy Hakobian, opened up nominations for the
  selection of Chair.

  A motion was made by Chair Cabot to nominate Commissioner Velazquez as Chair.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  VELAZQUEZ, HUERTA, CABOT, CORDERO, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  Staff congratulated Bronwyn Velazquez on her selection as Chair.

  Chair Velazquez opened up nominations for the selection of Vice Chair.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Cabot to nominate Commissioner Huerta as Vice Chair,
  motion seconded by Chair Velazquez.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  JUNE 7, 2021

  AYES:  VELAZQUEZ, HUERTA, CABOT, CORDERO, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  Staff congratulated Theresa Huerta on her selection as Vice-Chair.

 6. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. MONTHLY DEPARTMENT REPORT
  Community Services Supervisor, Christina Alatorre made the presentation.

  B. DATES TO REMEMBER
  Community Services Supervisor, Christina Alatorre made the presentation.

 7. COMMISSIONER COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/ MEETING REPORTS

  Commissioner Cabot thanked the department for all the events and creativity required to
  plan events. She is grateful to be on the commission.

  Vice Chair Huerta thanked Commissioner Cabot for asking great questions and making the
  commission meeting enjoyable. She also provided an update on the Mission. The roof
  construction should be completed next week.

  Chair Velazquez commended Commissioner Cabot for her service as Chair.

  Commissioner Cordero is excited and happy to join the Commission and see all our
  department has in store.

  Commissioner Xie thanks the commission for the welcome and looks forward to
  participating in summer events.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  October 4, 2021

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Community Services Department Staff

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Summer in Review 2021

During the pandemic, the department was able to offer programming that included swim
lessons, drive-in concerts and drive-in movies.

Aquatics
The Smith Park Pool staff did an outstanding job of coordinating programs and carrying
out their duties throughout the summer. The pool opened on June 15 and the
Community Services Department offered youth swim lessons, lap swim, recreational
swim, water aerobics, swim team and water polo pool reservations for the duration of
the summer. All local and state protocols were followed including limiting class sizes,
ensuring social distancing, and sanitation of all areas used by the public and staff.

Recreational Swim was offered on Tuesday nights, traditionally the most well attended
day of the week, for ten weeks throughout the summer. Participation ranged from 42 to
115 participants throughout the summer. New for 2021, registration was offered online
for a contactless registration process.

Swim lessons were modified for the first two cycles of summer, with staff teaching
swimming lessons from the deck, limiting class sizes and offerings. Staff transitioned in
the third cycle of summer from teaching on the deck to teaching swim lessons in the
water. For the duration of summer 2021, 546 participants were enrolled for youth and
adult swimming lessons.

San Gabriel Summer Camp
Staff were thrilled to offer San Gabriel’s Summer Camp in a modified format, following
all Department of Public Health Protocols, at the Adult Recreation Center. The program’s

  5-A
 lowest enrollment was during week one with 22 participants and the highest number of
enrollment was for week eight with 51 participants. The program was a great success,
with extremely positive feedback from parents. Additionally, due to staff’s attention to
detail, adherence to the County’s policies and cooperation from parents the camp did
not have a single COVID case.

Summer Concerts and Movies
The department offered three concerts and three movies at Vincent Lugo Park. One of the
concerts was in partnership with the San Gabriel Public Library geared toward the youth.

Recreation Coordinator, Amy Cortez, provided outdoor programming to the public that
ensured everyone felt comfortable attending the event, especially since this may be the
first time some attendees were in a group setting. Social distancing was enforced and
masks were encouraged.

  5-A
   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  October 4, 2021

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Community Services Department Staff

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Monthly Department Report

Aquatics
Regular Lap Swim is taking place on Monday and Wednesday evenings at Smith Park Pool
for the general public. San Gabriel Sea Gulls will host their Annual Halloween Meet in a
modified virtual format at Smith Park Pool on Saturday, October 30.

Contract Classes
Staff have done a tremendous job of working with instructors to provide classes that
meet the needs of the public in a safe and healthy manner. Classes were reintroduced in
person beginning in Spring 2021. The reception from participants was positive and were
thankful for measures staff took to ensure their safety.

Currently, masks are still required for indoor classes and social distancing is enforced.
Within the last two sessions staff have added pickleball, Crayola Art, and Kung Fu and
Tai Chi classes. Staff hope to expand the Tennis offerings through a partnership with
Johnny Allen Tennis during the winter sessions. The goal is to offer classes to the
youngest sector of our community as well as those of any age that are interested in
starting tennis at a remedial level.

The fall GUIDE was available in early September in a digital format. The fall GUIDE features
the Drive-Thru Trunk or Treat, Dumpling & Beer Fest, Turkey Trot, as well as our regularly
featured information on programs for older adults, youth, and activity classes. Staff has
begun work on the winter 2022 GUIDE. The issue will feature holiday events including
Holiday Tree Lighting, Lunar New Year, and regularly scheduled programming.

Facilities and Picnic Rentals
During the time the Community Services office was closed to the public, with the

  5-B
 exception of passport services and online class recordings, Community Services and
Public Works staff replaced the flooring in the entrance and dance room. Staff also
repainted these areas and installed new baseboards throughout the building. As we
reintroduce classes and community meetings the response to the changes have been
positive.

Facility rentals are in full force at the Adult Recreation Center with no openings until 2022.
The only modifications required by the County at this time is for guests to wear masks
while inside the facility. The department hopes to begin renting the Dance Room and the
North Room in 2022.

Staff have improved the reservation process for picnic rentals and have made it more
efficient for the customer and staff through an online form.

Older Adult Programs
Programming for older adults was paused for the last year in alignment with the LA
County Department of Public Health’s protocols, with the exception of the drive through
meal program with YWCA. However, with the June 15th reopening and the availability of
the vaccine and booster shots, staff is confident in reintroducing older adult programs
to the City. Programs that are returning include social bingo, health and education
lectures, table tennis, pickelball at Smith Park, and free art workshops.

Youth Programs
The after-school programs at Coolidge, McKinley, Washington and Wilson Elementary
Schools have commenced with attendance ranging from 25 to 45 participants each day.
Staff have done an excellent job planning and preparing activities and crafts for each
school site. In addition to program planning, staff are following all district COVID-19 safety
protocols. Staff have received positive feedback from school Principals in regards to the
program.

The Jefferson Middle School sports program has been modified to meet the COVID-19
protocols established by Los Angeles County Department of Public Health and the San
Gabriel Unified School District by offering a co-ed outdoor volleyball clinic. The program
began October 4. Registration is currently full with 15 participants. A second session will
be offered October 25. Staff have been trained in all district protocols, volleyball sports
coaching, and concussion training.

Special Events

  5-B
 Drive-Thru Trunk or Treat - On October 29 from 5:30 pm to 7:30 pm the Community
Services Department will host a Drive-Thru Trunk or Treat event, which will include local
community groups handing out candy with decorated booths and live music as
participants enter the parking lot. Pre-registration is required at sangabrielcity.com or by
calling the Community Services Department.

Virtual Costume Contest - Youth 12 years of age and under are welcome to enter the
virtual contest with their favorite costume. The contest will have three categories including
Spookiest, Home Made and Most Creative. Winners for each category will receive a gift
card/ certificate to a local business. Pre-registration is required at sangabrielcity.com or
by calling the Community Services Department.

46th Annual Turkey Trot- The 46th Annual Turkey Trot is scheduled for Saturday,
November 20 at 6:00 a.m. The race will begin and end at Vincent Lugo Park. Registration
includes race entry, a commemorative t-shirt and finisher medal, entry into the raffle and
refreshments. Top 3 winners in each age category will earn a special medal and each 1st
place finisher will receive a gift card for a turkey. Discounted registration is offered
through October 29, and can be made online at sangabrielcity.com.

Trips
The Department’s first in person trip took place on Friday, October 1. It was a day trip to
the Harvest Festival- Art and Craft Fair at the Ventura Fairgrounds. Fifteen people were
enrolled with one volunteer escort in attendance. The upcoming trips include a Whale
Watching Cruise and the Festival of Lights at Mission Inn. Trips for the winter season will
be announced in the upcoming weeks.
